For throat mics on a budget:

You're looking at about fifteen to thirty dollars for the generic ones on Amazon or AliExpress. They're PTT style — push-to-talk button, plugs into a three-point-five millimeter jack. Audio quality is usable, not amazing. Voice comes through clear enough, but it can sound a bit muffled or tinny compared to a regular mic. The build is cheap plastic, so they might not last forever with daily bike use.

For around fifty to sixty dollars you can get something like a COMMIXX brand throat mic. Better build, clearer audio, still lightweight. That's probably the sweet spot for your use case — not too expensive, but won't fall apart in a month.

The biggest thing to know is that all of them need some gain adjustment. Throat mics pick up quieter signals since they're reading vibrations, not air. You might need to boost the input level in your audio pipeline once you hook it up.

Want me to write up a short comparison you can check when you're ready to order?
